messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=real-time-inference, trigger=canary-2 error-rate>10% (5xx spike), rule=canary-rollout-healthcheck. Link: http://ops/redwood/incidents/1767005432

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident created INC-2026-789 (severity=high). Escalation policy: infra-oncall -> eng-platform. Notifying primary on-call.

maria: noticed the canary rollout started ~5m ago. Canary-2 shows ~18% 5xx and p95 latency up 400ms. Same binary as release v2026.03.

alex: acked INC-2026-789. I'm primary oncall, taking ownership. @maria can you paste the canary config and recent deploy command?

maria: here — deploy script output: ```sha: abc1234
coord: rollout 10%->25% canary-2
flags: enable-kvcache=true
``` Also tail from canary: ```ERROR model_runner: kvcache miss exception: KeyError('kv-idx')
```. 

jamal: seeing similar stack in qps logs from the same region (us-west-2). Might be a kernel path for quantized kernels. We'll check kernel selection logs.

serena: alex — do you want us to divert traffic to stable now? Risk of more customer impact if it ramps to 50%.

alex: yes please. Plan: 1) divert all traffic off canary-2 -> stable 100% 2) abort further rollout 3) investigate root cause on canary hosts 4) if needed, rollback canary image to prior sha. Executing step 1 now.

maria: running trafficctl command: ```trafficctl set-weight --route realtime-inference --target canary-2 0 && trafficctl set-weight --route realtime-inference --target stable 100```

maria: command output: `OK: weights applied (canary-2=0, stable=100)`

pd-bot: INC-2026-789: status update: mitigation action detected (traffic diversion). Notifying stakeholders and canceling further escalations for now.

tina-cs: CS update — we received ~7 customer reports in the last 10m complaining about request errors (IDs: C-224, C-225, C-231...). No P0 support pages yet but CS is patching templated messages.

alex: confirmation checks: canary-2 error-rate -> now 2%, stable still has small blips but overall p95 back to baseline. Nice work. Next: do we want to rollback canary-2 image or disable the new kernel flag? Thoughts?

jamal: initial suspicion: quant kernel path injected by the new runtime selection is hitting an uninitialized KV offset when sequence length > 2048. Quick mitigation: disable quant-kernel selection for canary release or revert to previous runtime config.

maria: I can flip the runtime flag per-cluster if we want. `infractl set-cluster-flag canary-2 runtime.force_legacy_kernels=true` — will apply in ~30s.

serena: recommend to revert the rollout entirely and mark canary-2 nodes for deeper diagnostics offline. If runtime flag flip fixes it, we can attempt a guarded restart.

alex: decision: keep diverted traffic, mark rollout paused, flip runtime flag on canary-2 and schedule a rollback if errors reappear. maria go ahead. I'll open an incident bridge and assign follow-ups.

maria: applied: `runtime.force_legacy_kernels=true` to canary-2 clusters. Logs show new sessions pick legacy path. Monitoring...

incident-bot: Bridge opened: https://bridge.redwood/incident/1767005432 — owner=alex, severity=high, impact="canary rollout caused transient 5xx for subset of traffic; diverted"

pd-bot: INC-2026-789: acked by alex. Next escalation window halted. Please add timeline entries and owners.

alex: timeline note — 1767005432: alert fired; 1767005450: ack; 1767005480: traffic diverted; 1767005520: runtime flag flipped; 1767005740: error-rate reduced to <3%. Assigned jamal for root-cause, maria for rollout automation fix, tina-cs for customer comms, serena for postmortem.

jamal: collecting host dumps from canary-2 nodes, will run binary diff between v2026.03 and previous. Suspect kernel selection table mismatch in quant path.

tina-cs: prepping a CS advisory for affected customers: short explanation + ETA for follow-up. If situation persists I'll escalate to P0. For now we're monitoring. :white_check_mark: 

alex: excellent. Once jamal posts root-cause evidence we'll decide rollback vs patch. For now keep diversion and keep the bridge open. If any upward trends, page PD again.

serena: leaving reminder: add the release tag, canary config, and telemetry dashboard links to the postmortem. Also check canary gating thresholds — looks like 10%->25% jump was a bit aggressive for new kernel selection.

maria: noted. I'll pin the deploy script and logs in the bridge. Moving to post-incident actions: set rollout default ramp steps to max 10% increments and require kernel smoke tests before a canary.

alex: closing updates for now — moving to investigation mode. Will send final incident summary once root cause is confirmed. Thanks everyone. :pray:
